h1: Pajamas Koh Chang — a design hostel with a pool two minutes from Klong Prao Beach
intro: If you still picture hostels as bare rooms with beds in a row, take a look at Pajamas Koh Chang first · this is a stylish design hostel built around a courtyard swimming pool, tucked down a side lane off the main Klong Prao road, about a 2-minute walk to the beach · it mixes dorm beds for backpackers with private rooms for couples and families, plus a common lounge with a pool table and sofas and a breakfast cafe that guests rave about (the pancakes come up a lot) · from approx. ฿550/night for a dorm bed · this review is compiled from real guest reviews — we did not stay there ourselves.

body.html: Pajamas has been open since 2014 and has become a name backpackers on Koh Chang know well · what sets it apart from the usual budget guesthouse is design — its 29 rooms are arranged around a central courtyard pool, finished in warm wood and raw concrete with an easygoing, surfer-style vibe · plenty of guests say they were pleasantly surprised on arrival because it looks better than the price suggests · the most recent renovation in 2020 keeps the rooms feeling fresh and clean.

The location is a real advantage · Pajamas sits down a small lane off the main Klong Prao road, about a 2-minute walk to the sand, dropping you onto a long stretch of beach that many rate as one of the best on the island · local restaurants and seafood spots like Nong Bua are within walking distance, with a 7-Eleven and small shops nearby · you can get by without transport, though renting a motorbike makes exploring the rest of the island far easier.

"So easy to meet people — the common area has a pool table and games · the Western breakfast was awesome, probably the best pancakes I've ever had · and the beach is just a short walk. Incredible value."

The heart of Pajamas is its social atmosphere · the common area is an open-sided lounge running into the cafe, with a pool table, a punching bag, a widescreen TV, sofas, ukuleles, board games and books · it's where solo travellers naturally end up chatting and making friends · real guest reviews agree the staff are warm and helpful, serving fresh coffee and breakfast at wooden tables in the airy cafe · the courtyard pool isn't large, but it's just right for a cooling dip after a day on the beach.

There's a good spread of room types · on the budget side are dorm beds, both mixed and female-only, with bunk beds that have privacy curtains and personal reading lights · on the private side there are Deluxe Double rooms with pool views and Group/Family configurations for travelling in numbers · every room has air-conditioning, quality bedding and a modern bathroom · one thing to know: the upper dorm bunks need a ladder, so request a lower bunk at booking if that's not for you.

Now for the honest part · because this is a hostel built around a sociable vibe, it can get noisy around the pool when it's busy, so it isn't ideal if you need total quiet · the private rooms, while nicely styled, are fairly compact compared with a mid-range hotel · some reviews note that the website photos can make rooms look more 'deluxe' than a hostel really is, and a few guests mention stained sheets on occasion · the lane down to the beach can look a bit scruffy in places, which is the lane rather than the property · and there are no resort-style amenities here such as a spa or gym.

The bottom line: Pajamas Koh Chang is one of the best-value design hostels on Klong Prao Beach — walkable to the sand, better-looking than its price, friendly enough to make new friends, and with a breakfast people remember · it suits solo travellers, budget-minded couples and anyone who prefers a lively stay over private quiet · if you want full privacy or a full set of resort amenities, this may not be the right fit.

honestChecks: If you want peace, quiet and full privacy — this place leans sociable and the pool area can get loud when busy → consider a quiet beachfront resort instead.
If you're travelling as a family wanting a roomy space — the private rooms are fairly compact → look at the Group/Family rooms here, or compare resorts with larger rooms in a similar price range.
If you're booking a dorm bed — the upper bunks need a ladder → request a lower bunk at booking and pack earplugs for busier nights.

tips.body: Upper bunks need a ladder · if that's awkward or you arrive late, request a lower bunk at booking or mention it at the front desk.

tips.title: Don't skip breakfast
tips.body: The cafe's pancakes and fresh coffee come up again and again in reviews · order a Western breakfast and enjoy it at a wooden table in the airy cafe.

tips.title: Rent a motorbike to explore
tips.body: The beach is walkable, but for waterfalls, other beaches and restaurants further out, a motorbike from the tour desk is far handier.

tips.title: Pack earplugs in high season
tips.body: The sociable pool and common area can run late when it's busy · earplugs make for an easier night's sleep.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Pajamas Koh Chang

faq.q: Where is Pajamas Koh Chang, and is it far from the beach?
faq.a: It sits down a small lane off the main Klong Prao road, about a 2-minute walk to the beach · Klong Prao is a long sandy stretch many rate as one of the best on Koh Chang · local restaurants, seafood spots and a 7-Eleven are all within walking distance.

faq.q: How much does Pajamas Koh Chang cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: From approx. ฿550/night for a bed in a mixed dormitory · options include mixed dorms, a female-only dorm, a Group Six room, and private Deluxe Double rooms with pool views (around ฿2,300/night) · prices vary by season and platform, so compare a few before booking.

faq.q: Does Pajamas Koh Chang have a swimming pool?
faq.a: Yes · it's a courtyard pool that the 29 rooms are arranged around · it isn't large, but it's perfect for a cooling dip after the beach · a pool is a rare extra for a hostel in this price range on Koh Chang.

faq.q: Who is Pajamas Koh Chang best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for solo travellers, budget-minded couples and anyone who likes a lively stay · the social vibe and common areas make it easy to meet people, and it looks better than the price · if you want full privacy and quiet or resort-style amenities, it may not be the right fit.

faq.q: What is breakfast like at Pajamas Koh Chang?
faq.a: There's an on-site cafe serving a continental breakfast (charged separately) · the pancakes and fresh coffee are repeatedly praised in reviews · you eat at wooden tables in the airy cafe that opens onto the common area — a relaxed start to the day.
